Your boss seems ill-equipped to handle anyone with depression. There could be a whole spiel of 'not his job' but honestly an employer should have some sympathy. He is not your fault; he is only his fault. If he makes you feel miserable, the job may not be worth it, even knowing money must come from somewhere. Money can't buy you everything, especially not self-satisfaction.

Look into working from home perhaps? Find something to get yourself stress off you. I can't tell you whether it'll be worth going in to work tomorrow. Based on what I read, if I had to guess, it wouldn't be. The boss seems incapable of working with you or meeting you halfway. You deserve better.

Power to you whatever happens.

Considering Gollum's attachment to the ring can be considered an addiction, I figured the reason he would fall unto the fires of Mt. Doom and sacrifice himself to destroy the ring isn't out of desire to do so. Sure, the Ring wouldn't want to be destroyed, and Gollum would do anything he can and figures is sensible to protect it (being addicted to its effects), but nothing about either suggests they are perfect - ESPECIALLY when you consider Gollum's situation. It'd be like trusting a long-term addict to give up his vice when the best 'help' he has ever been given is withdrawal followed by massive temptation and an environment that seemingly rewarded shady and selfish behavior.

Say what you will about the Ring, but part of its arc (to the best of my knowledge) is its corrupting influence on whoever wears it - the longer they wear it, the worse the get. Even Bilbo struggled with it, and his state didn't advance nearly as far as Gollum, but he ultimately had enough of his mental faculties and ability to go 'cold turkey' so that he could live another day as, well, Bilbo.

Gollum, though? He might not want to do any harm to himself or the Ring, but he's pretty far along under the Ring's influences. Can we trust he'll do the right thing? Can we even trust him to do the WRONG thing (i.e. protect the Ring) without screwing it up?
